tool_input.message:
Verdict: FAIL. Fixes 1 and 2 are correct. Fix 3 (isOperationalExecFailure) is correctly inverted in isolation, but its integration with pgp.CheckKeyExpiry has a real, reproduced hole. Send back for round 3.

**1. parseColonExpiry timestamp comparison (internal/pgp/expiry.go:133-142) — PASS.**
`exp <= now` is the right boundary: treating a key expiring at exactly the current second as already-expired is the conservative, fail-closed choice (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's design invariant), and the edge case is unobservable in practice anyway (no way to reliably hit the same Unix second between generation and check). `TestCheckKeyExpiry_Expired` proves it with a real 3-second-expiry key and a 5s sleep — genuine gpg round trip, not a fixture.

**2. classifyStatusLines EXPKEYSIG/EXPSIG (internal/daemon/signature.go:343-355) — PASS.**
Precedence (NO_PUBKEY > GOODSIG > EXPKEYSIG > BADSIG/ERRSIG/REVKEYSIG/EXPSIG > default) is correct and tested against a real gpg 2.4.4 EXPKEYSIG capture (`TestVerifyDetachedSignature_ExpiredKey`, live end-to-end). EXPKEYSIG can't legitimately co-occur with something that should outrank it — it requires the key to have been *found and verified*, which is mutually exclusive with NO_PUBKEY, and gpg emits one primary verdict line per signature. EXPSIG → ReasonInvalid is the right domain call: an expired signature needs re-signing, not key renewal, so bucketing it with BADSIG/ERRSIG/REVKEYSIG (not ReasonKeyExpired) matches the remediation path.

**3. isOperationalExecFailure — the predicate itself is correct; a caller breaks its contract. FAIL.**

The function's own structure (nil/*exec.ExitError = ran-to-completion; `errors.Is(err, pgp.ErrKeyExpiryFinding)` checked first = positive identification of a domain result; everything else = operational) is genuinely exhaustive as a standalone predicate. I confirmed the double-`%w` sentinel wrap is sound Go (empirically, not from memory):

```
wrapped := fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrSentinel, inner)
errors.Is(wrapped, ErrSentinel) → true
errors.Is(wrapped, inner)       → true
```

Go 1.20+ supports multiple `%w` verbs via the multi-error tree; this repo is on go 1.26 (go.mod), so it's supported. I also checked `internal/pgp/sign.go`'s two existing `CheckKeyExpiry` callers (lines 34, 77) — both only test `err != nil`, so the sentinel-wrapping change is transparent to them. No regression there.

**But the ordering question you asked ("could a wrapped error match both sentinel and *exec.ExitError") surfaces a real bug — not in the order, in what CheckKeyExpiry hands the helper.**

`CheckKeyExpiry` (internal/pgp/expiry.go:64-66) does this on ANY `cmd.Run()` failure:
```go
if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("gpg list-keys %q: %w: %s", keyID, err, stderr.String())
}
```
This is unconditional — it never distinguishes "process never started" from "process ran and exited non-zero." Compare this to the other two exec.Command sites in signature.go (`assertSingleOwnerKey`, `verifyDetachedSignature`), which both parse `stdout` regardless of exit code specifically because gpg exits non-zero for legitimate domain outcomes (key not found, bad signature) — `isOperationalExecFailure` there only gates "did the process run," never "should I trust the exit code." `CheckKeyExpiry` doesn't follow that pattern: on any non-nil `cmd.Run()` error it just forwards, unparsed, un-sentinel-wrapped.

I reproduced this empirically. `gpg --list-keys <not-in-keyring>` exits status 2 (a real `*exec.ExitError`, confirmed live: `gpg: error reading key: No public key`, exit 2). Feeding that through `CheckKeyExpiry` on an empty homedir:

```
err = gpg list-keys "[redacted-email]": exit status 2: gpg: error reading key: No public key
errors.Is(ErrKeyExpiryFinding) = false   <- not sentinel-wrapped, CheckKeyExpiry never got to parseColonExpiry
errors.As(*exec.ExitError)     = true    <- but it DOES contain *exec.ExitError
```

Run through `isOperationalExecFailure`: sentinel check fails (correctly — this was never routed through the success path), then `errors.As(err, &exitErr)` succeeds, so the function returns `false` (not operational). In `VerifySignature` (signature.go:151-156) that means: `return &SignatureError{Reason: ReasonKeyExpired, ...}` — a key-not-found failure gets classified and audit-logged as **key-expired**, which is factually wrong.

This is exactly the defect class this mission exists to close — an incomplete completeness contract at a call site — just moved one layer down, from `isOperationalExecFailure`'s own body (fixed) into `CheckKeyExpiry`'s error-shape contract with it (still broken). The helper's exhaustiveness assumes every caller either (a) genuinely never parses on failure (operational), or (b) always parses stdout regardless of exit code and only sentinel-wraps a *real* domain finding. `CheckKeyExpiry` does neither consistently — it parses only on `err == nil`, and forwards every `cmd.Run()` failure identically whether it's a start failure or a completed-but-nonzero run.

**Blast radius in the current call graph:** narrow but real. `VerifySignature` only reaches `CheckKeyExpiry` after `importOwnerKey` → `assertSingleOwnerKey` has already confirmed exactly one match for `ownerKeyID` in that same freshly-created, single-use `gpgHome` (signature.go:141-150). So the "key not found" branch shouldn't fire in the intended sequence — it would need the key to vanish between two sequential exec calls against a keyring nothing else touches, e.g. a transient gpg-agent hiccup that also happens to produce exit 2. Not an authorization bypass (the command is still rejected either way — fails closed), but it does violate the "genuinely correct classification" bar this mission is chartered to hit, and mislabels the audit-log reason for what would be a genuinely unusual gpg failure. Also worth noting: `VerifySignature` isn't wired into any command-execution call site yet (grep confirms `signature.go` is the only non-test caller) — so today this is latent, not live — but it's a security-critical trust boundary and will be load-bearing once wired in.

**Recommended fix:** make `CheckKeyExpiry` symmetric with `assertSingleOwnerKey`/`verifyDetachedSignature` — split its own `cmd.Run()` outcome the same way (nil or `*exec.ExitError` → call `parseColonExpiry(stdout.String(), keyID)` regardless of exit code; anything else → forward unwrapped as a true operational failure). `parseColonExpiry`'s existing `pubCount == 0` branch ("key not found in gpg output") already exists and is currently *dead* for real gpg invocations — it's only reachable today via `TestParseColonExpiry`'s direct fixture calls, never through `CheckKeyExpiry`'s real gpg path, because `cmd.Run()` fails first on genuine exit-2. This one change makes it live, keeps `pgp` self-contained (no need to import daemon's helper — same nil-or-ExitError split, done locally), and every domain outcome — including "not found" — flows through the existing `ErrKeyExpiryFinding` sentinel wrap, which `isOperationalExecFailure` already handles correctly.

**4. Fail-closed end-to-end for a genuinely expired key — PASS, both paths confirmed.**
`TestCheckKeyExpiry_Expired` (real 3s-expiry key, gpg exits 0, `parseColonExpiry` finds the passed timestamp) proves CheckKeyExpiry's gate catches it before `gpg --verify` ever runs — this is the live path. `TestVerifyDetachedSignature_ExpiredKey` proves the EXPKEYSIG path independently by calling `verifyDetachedSignature` directly, bypassing the CheckKeyExpiry gate — the test's own comment correctly notes this is the *only* way to still reach EXPKEYSIG in practice, since the gate preempts it in the real `VerifySignature` flow. Both reject correctly. The gap in #3 doesn't threaten this invariant — it only affects the *label* on an already-rejected command in a scenario outside the intended call sequence.

Net: don't close. One precise fix needed in `internal/pgp/expiry.go`'s `CheckKeyExpiry`, plus a test proving a "key not found via non-zero exit" `CheckKeyExpiry` call classifies as operational=false-but-not-ReasonKeyExpired... actually more precisely: a test proving it now flows through `parseColonExpiry` and gets sentinel-wrapped with a "not found" detail rather than silently matching the exit-nonzero-as-domain heuristic by accident. Happy to detail the exact test shape if useful.

tool_input.new_string:
**`REVKEYSIG` folds into `ReasonInvalid` rather than becoming a fifth
reason.** A revoked owner key and a forged or corrupted signature call for
the identical operator response under this design: stop trusting the key
immediately and re-provision through `beadle init` (§ Migration, item 5).
That is unlike `ReasonKeyExpired`, which is a routine hygiene gap the
operator can plan a rotation around — a revocation means the owner (or
whoever holds the owner's revocation certificate) has already declared the
key untrustworthy, which is closer in kind to "this signature should not be
trusted" than to "this key needs renewing." Splitting it into its own reason
would add a branch to every future caller's remediation logic (the daemon
startup loader, the audit-log entry writer) without changing what that
caller does differently in response. `Detail` still carries gpg's own
status text, so a human reading an audit entry or a log line can tell a
`REVKEYSIG` outcome apart from a `BADSIG` even though `Reason` collapses
them to the same value.

**`EXPKEYSIG` and `EXPSIG` were found missing during implementation, not
designed here originally.** `CheckKeyExpiry` (§4) is meant to catch an
expired owner key before `gpg --verify` ever runs, but a full-diff review
after implementation found that its original form only checked that an
expiry field was *present*, never that the date it named had actually
passed — so an already-expired key reached `gpg --verify` regardless, which
emits `EXPKEYSIG` (not `GOODSIG`) for a signature that is otherwise valid
but made by an expired key. Fixed in both places: `CheckKeyExpiry` now
compares the expiry timestamp against the current time (closing the gate
this section always intended), and `classifyStatusLines` gained an explicit
`EXPKEYSIG` → `ReasonKeyExpired` case as defense in depth for the rare path
that still reaches `gpg --verify` directly. `EXPSIG` — a signature that
itself carries an expiration, a different gpg feature from key expiry —
folds into `ReasonInvalid` alongside `BADSIG`/`ERRSIG`/`REVKEYSIG`: none of
those outcomes mean "the key needs renewing," they mean "do not trust this
signature."
